Ask most people today what a "blue moon" is and they'll probably say it's the second full moon in a month. That definition was a mistake which came about in the 1930s when an astronomical article found it too complex to explain the original definition in the space allotted for printing.

A year is divided into four astronomical seasons, from equinox to solstice and then from solstice to equinox, twice a year. There are usually 12 moons in a year, though every few years there is a 13th moon. The full moons also were named. For example, the three full moons of Spring are the Pink, Flower and Strawberry moons.

Every few years, an astronomical season will have four full moons. The first two keep their names, the last one keeps its name, and the extra one, the third in the season, gets the special name of Blue Moon. This spring's "Pink Moon" occurred just after the March Equinox. Then in April, we had the Flower Moon. This full moon is a Blue Moon, leaving the full moon just before the Solstice in June to be the Strawberry Moon.
A true "blue moon" - This full moon in May 2016 is a blue moon by the older definition. The next true blue moon will be in May 2019
